column3: Package manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop-testkit v0.2.1-rc.2: ESM, peer-only workspace deps (cordis, dsh-agent, dsh-agent-loop, dsh-session, dsh-session-projection, dsh-system-prompt, dsh-tools, dsh-working-directory, dsh-fs-local), publishes lib/index.js + lib/types.
Bilingual-pair hash record for the agent-loop-testkit README: one 16-hex digest per heading section for en and zh, with the `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <file>` command to re-record.

English doc for the testkit: mounts six prerequisite services in a fixed order, stops before AgentLoop so callers own load order, offers createInboxStub/unsupportedInbox, and states "no model-visible behavior / no KV cache effect".
Chinese mirror of the agent-loop-testkit README; same structure and anchors, line-for-line counterpart of README.md.

Two Inbox doubles over process-local arrays: createInboxStub (mutable next-turn/next-step queues with locate/splice/replace/remove) and unsupportedInbox (every mutation throws "this test Agent does not support Inbox mutations").

Mounting API: mountAgentLoopTestDependencies mounts LlmRuntime, SessionStore, SessionProjectionRegistry, SystemPrompt, [FsLocal+WorkingDirectory], ToolRuntime, AgentRegistry; mountAgentLoopTestHarness mounts the production AgentLoop and exposes create() plus a narrow claim() driver.
provideWorkingDirectoryFixture: ctx.provide('workingDirectory') with a get/ensure pair that reads session.header.cwd ?? defaultDirectory and resolves without touching the filesystem.

Spec proving: unsupported Inbox throws, the configurable prerequisite spine mounts (systemPrompt personaPrefix + tools mode native reach the real renderer), an existing FsLocal is kept, the mutable stub's queue semantics, and a production Agent's durable inbox events, duplicate rejection, invalid-splice rejection and claim ordering.

tsconfig extending tsconfig.base.json with rootDir src/outDir lib/types and project references to cordis, agent, agent-loop, llm, session, system-prompt, tools, session-projection, working-directory, fs-local.

Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-test-runtime: browser test runtime with dev-only deps on @testing-library/react, js-yaml, vitest and peer deps on the whole client stack plus @deepseek-ai/dsh-remote-mock.
Per-section en/zh digests for the client-runtime README (20 sections incl. the four `use-this-package` anchors and the lifecycle section).

English doc for the two client tiers: the jsdom SlotTestRuntime bench (declare/mount/renderSlot/dispose) and the whole-client TestClient tier (web roster booted through production bootClient over a RemoteMock); documents the "Model Experience: none / KV cache: none" contract and known limits.

Chinese mirror of the client-runtime README, including the same known-limitations list (proxy calls bypass Gateway invoke, undeclared endpoints are unary misses, node ambient types added, Session/Conversation/Chat fixtures kept separate).
allowAllAccess props + allowAllAccessPlugin: provides an always-true `remoteAccess` service and a root keyedHook so ui-session/ui-workspace publish allow-everything access Hooks.

Reads the real web profile's browser roster out of the bundles' own `dsh.bundle.patch` files using the include plugin's entryListSchema/applyEntryPatches, honouring nested Loader groups and `disabled` JS expressions; throws where the launcher only warns.

Deep-import-only barrel for the whole-client tier (ClientRoster, TestClient, remoteDefaultResponses, bundleRoster/webApp, createClientTest), deliberately kept out of the package root so slot-tier specs never load it.

Imports every roster row's `/client` namespace in process and registers them as pre-arrived factories on a production ClientModuleSystem, so neither the Loader's internal.import nor a prefetch ever fetches a bundle; the modules bootstrap row cannot be provided.

Table of default Remote answers for every endpoint the web assembly calls at boot (session/list, settings/describe, session/modelCatalog, agentPresets/list, dynamicCordisRunner/*, credentials/describe, account/*), each row commented with the plugin that calls it; `$events` lives in RemoteMock.

Provides `remote.<ns>` services as Proxies over the roster's own Connection: a call becomes endpoint `<ns>/<method>`, a stream when the mock registered a stream script, and a unary rejection is folded into gateway/internal or gateway/cancelled exactly like the generated client.

ClientRoster: immutable ordered rows with pick/closure/without (closure walks inject edges and stops at PLATFORM_SEED), graphFromRoster synthesizes a one-batch WebBootGraph with placeholder plugin URLs, and assertPlan rejects `provide` keys outside the roster.

TestClient.start: loads the roster modules, binds the RemoteMock to the client's Connection, holds shared jsdom shims (EventSource/ResizeObserver/document.fonts) with refcounted install/remove, boots production bootClient, optionally mounts the renderer, waits for connection, and on teardown reports unmatched Remote calls even when the plugin tree also failed to dispose.

createClientTest: a Vitest test.extend with a fresh RemoteMock preloaded with remoteDefaultResponses, a lazy `start()` that shares one promise, and teardown that disposes the client and asserts no unmatched requests even when no client was started.

stubConfigForm: an in-memory settings scope starting in the loading state with vi.fn spies for set/mutate/unset, a listener set, a publish() that mimics a Host acceptance, and listenerCount() for disposal assertions.

Fixture shapes: sessionSnapshot (complete quiescent Session Controller state), conversationSnapshot, chatSnapshot, workspaceSnapshot, plus SessionBehaviorOverrides typed against the production ISession so a face change breaks the fixture at compile time.

SlotTestRuntime: assembles the real Cordis Context, SlotRegistry, ui-session adapter and UI renderer around test-owned Session/Workspace doubles; owns declare/mount/renderSlot/storeOf, an idempotent dispose (unmount views, dispose features, release scopes, clear localStorage) and the OwnerPropsCell that drives React through useSyncExternalStore.
usePinnedBrowserLanguages: a beforeEach/afterEach pair that pins navigator.languages/language so a spec asserting localized copy states the browser it assumes instead of inheriting the machine's.

TestRemote: a ctx.remote double providing $on subscriptions driven by an explicit emit(), a mutable $host, one service per scripted namespace, and a $mount that always rejects ("needs the real Client Remote service"); it deliberately lets a throwing listener propagate.

TestSessions/FixtureSession: a fail-loud Session face (every unstubbed verb throws naming itself), a MutableSessionEventSource, identity-stable per-key projection faces, catalog rows that outlive references, and lazily minted real-tagged scopes whose lifetime is an AbortController aborted on release.

domSnapshotSerializer: folds CSS-module class hashes (`_frame_334d2d` -> `frame`) back to their local name and collapses <svg> internals to a data-content FNV-1a fingerprint, working on a clone so the live DOM keeps its class/tag queries.
makeTranslate: a translate stub over plain dictionaries mirroring LocaleRuntime's resolution order (first dictionary owning the key wins, else the key stays) and its `{name}` interpolation.

TestWorkspaces: implements the production IWorkspaces face so a Controller change breaks the double at compile time; every action is recorded in `calls`, defaults are inert echoes, and `stub(method, impl)` replaces one action's behaviour.
Vitest snapshot file with two DOM snapshots showing the normalized class names and the svg data-content fingerprint, plus a childless svg left untouched.

Proves the roster really comes from the shipped bundles: dsh-base then dsh-web-app compose, no dangling inject edges, browser rows carry their declarations, and a scratch installation resolves bundle dependencies from real package directories (with linked bundles and uneven node_modules search paths).

Shows that a real bundle dependency closure activates its requested client plugins with no extra roster rows: HMR boots with its module provider and no Connection, and the Session Controller boots with its file-upload provider and reaches the ready phase.

Proves in-process module arrival: dynamic /client imports resolve, a provided row replaces one, the bootstrap row is pinned, a missing import is prefixed with the package name, and the vendored Loader boots over the table with every entry active and no bundle fetched.
Unit spec for assertPlan: a bare roster and roster-owned `provide` keys are accepted, and a key outside the roster is rejected with the roster listed.

Spec for the remote.<ns> proxies: namespace discovery from roster injects (both array and object forms) plus mock endpoints, routing calls through the mock, folding a ruleless call into gateway/internal and an aborted call into gateway/cancelled, and passing stream items and failures through unchanged.

Spec for ClientRoster and graphFromRoster: frozen copies, duplicate refusal, order-preserving pick/without/closure, the platform-seed exception, unknown-name errors, and that the synthesized graph passes the production parseBootManifest validator.

Node-environment spec for TestClient: boots and connects without a DOM, closes the client even when teardown fails (and still rethrows), rethrows a row that fails to apply, refuses to provide the generated-Remote rows, reports unmatched requests alongside a failed teardown, and refuses to mount without a DOM.

jsdom spec for TestClient: boots the whole web-app roster and mounts it, leaves pre-existing globals alone and removes only its own shims, and reports the mock log when the connection never becomes ready.

Spec that the Vitest fixture's cleanup stays active after an assertion failure and without a started client, that concurrent starts share one promise, and that a rejected startup is kept with its caller and releases the page transport.

Spec for the fixture helpers: allow-all access hooks, the always-true remoteAccess service, retraction of default root sources without removing live replacements, pane/workspace behaviour, and scope borrowing/disposal.

Spec for TestRemote's own contract: subscription and disposal, an inert emit for an unsubscribed name, the $mount refusal, scripted namespaces reachable as ctx.remote.<name>, and the refusal of a namespace that would shadow a double member.

48-case spec for SlotTestRuntime against the production SlotRegistry + createSlotRenderer: root declaration and rendering, SessionProvider/reference lifecycle, lazily minted real-tagged scopes, per-session store identity and isolation, workspace feed, feature mount/dispose cascade, slot-local views, the fail-loud session face, and the stubbed settings scope.
Client tsconfig extending tsconfig.base.client.json with the node/client-build-environment ambient types and 22 project references across the client, api, core and typert packages.
One-line tsdown config reusing the shared clientLibrary() helper for the lib/types/index.js entry.
Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-mock-server: zero runtime dependencies, only cordis as a peer/dev dependency, publishing lib/index.js.
Per-section en/zh digests for the llm-mock-server README, including the random-mode, timing-and-content-controls and wire-flow sections.

English doc for the fault server: the full behavior table (connection_reset, stream_disconnect, partial_disconnect, stall, empty, empty_body/stream_eof/partial_eof, malformed_json/event, 429/5xx/503, auth/invalid/context_overflow/quota, success/reasoning/tool_call/max_tokens/slow_success, wrong_content_type, random) plus the rule that one accepted request consumes exactly one behavior.
Chinese mirror of the llm-mock-server README; same behavior table and the same "random weights model test pressure, not production incidence" limitation.

Standalone process wrapper: parses argv, prints a JSONL `unavailable` record and delays the bind for connection_refused, prints a `ready` record with the /v1 base URL and seed, tees request/result events as JSONL to stdout, and exits 130/143 on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Dependency-free CLI parser over node:util parseArgs: --sequence (connection_refused allowed first only), --listen-delay-ms/--repeat-last/--seed/--random-weights, timing and content flags, and cross-option constraints (a nonzero port for connection_refused, random required for --seed).

Mock Messages server: 24 named behaviors, an arrival-ordered FIFO cursor that advances only after validation, seeded weighted random selection (mulberry32), per-request records with body/headers/chunksSent/outcome, SSE writers for the Messages wire, and idempotent close() that force-terminates stalled connections.

Spec for the CLI parser: help without a sequence, every option parsed, standalone defaults, the default 750 ms unavailable interval, a reproducible weighted random profile, and 23 rejected-argv cases (tokenizer errors vs bounds probes).

Spec for the wire behaviors: the success transcript and its event telemetry, gateway-prefix support, observer failures ignored, five truncation/malformation behaviors asserted by chunk count, the three transport-boundary behaviors, stall plus idempotent close, client-closed recording, UTF-8 split across request chunks, IPv6 base URL, the structured HTTP errors with retry-after rounding, script exhaustion/repeat-last, seeded random reproducibility, and that invalid requests do not consume the script.
Minimal tsconfig extending tsconfig.base.json with rootDir src/outDir lib/types and no project references.
tsdown config building lib/types/index.js as one self-contained ESM node file with code splitting off.
Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-replay: depends on dsh-session-format-catalog and dsh-util-values, peers on cordis/compaction/deepseek-llm-api-extensions (optional)/llm/session.
Per-section en/zh digests for the llm-replay README, including the nested-agents and binding-and-stream-flow sections.

English doc for the keyless replay plugin: the config table (file/overrideFile/childFiles/providers/paceMs), how the projected fixture is parsed and migrated, the first-call-order binding of parent and child scripts, the two failure modes that need a replay.override.json sidecar, and the known limit that concurrent sibling subagents bind non-deterministically.
Chinese mirror of the llm-replay README; same fixture rules, same sidecar semantics, same two known limitations.

The whole replay plugin: fixture parsing/migration through the build-static format catalog, deriveReplayScript (one chunks entry per durable Assistant settlement; a stream without a finish chunk is the fingerprint of a thrown stream), the override sidecar validator, {{fromRequest:<regex>}} placeholder resolution against the live request, per-session script binding by first-call order, and assertConsumed() at teardown.

2344-line spec driving the plugin through the REAL LlmRuntime waterfall: derive/parse/load helpers, v0-v1-v2-v3 fixture migration, prepareSessionSnapshotFixtureForComparison, the throw/hang/chunks override kinds, the unrecorded-session and script-exhausted errors, HMR-safe listener disposal, DeepSeek request-extension acceptance, and per-session binding.
Exact inventory of deliberate historical conversion refusals (path, source version, exact reason string) plus the list of headerless snapshot-harness protocol fixtures that are exempt from migration.

Restores every committed versioned session*.jsonl under snapshots/, packages/ and scripts/snapshots/python-sdk-single-exe/ through the real catalog without changing source bytes, and pins each deliberate refusal by exact reason; a policy block checks the refusal classifier itself.
tsconfig extending tsconfig.base.json with references to cosmokit, cordis, compaction, llm, deepseek-llm-api-extensions, session and session-format-catalog.
Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke: execa and tsx as runtime deps, peers on cordis/agent/llm/session/http-proxy, dev-dep on app-boot.
Per-section en/zh digests for the loader-smoke README (8 sections).

English doc for the loader-smoke harness: runLoaderSmoke's ownership (isolated cwd, DSH homes, diagnostics, deadline, termination, EOF, cleanup), the src-vs-lib launch modes, the shipped-profile helper, runFixtureTurn, and the limits (built mode needs a prior build, execa's 100 MB maxBuffer, timeout kills only the direct child).
Chinese mirror of the loader-smoke README; same ownership statement and the same three known limits.

runFixtureTurn: waits for exactly one configured root agent to publish, sends a user message, observes only the owned session's events until the durable inbox receipt, accumulates per-step usage keyed by turn/step, waits for agent idle, flushes the session, and returns the final assistant text plus usage.

Shared subprocess harness: resolveExampleMode (absent/''/src -> src, anything else throws), resolveExampleLaunch (src mode runs the TS bin under tsx with TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH; lib mode runs the derived lib/bin.js under plain Node), and runLoaderSmoke (isolated temp cwd, cleared proxy env, 30 s diagnostic timeout with SIGKILL, expected-exit-code check, optional prepare/inspect hooks).

Spec for runFixtureTurn against a hand-built Context double: rejects zero or multiple roots, waits for agent/created before requiring one, observes only the owned interval, deduplicates usage, returns no usage when the interval records none, and always removes its listener when the turn fails.

Spec for the mode-aware launch resolver: src mode's --import tsx plus TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH, the missing-tsconfig refusal, the app-specific tsx hook, lib mode's derived lib bin with no tsx and no paths env, the Windows path derivation, the "no /src/ segment" refusal, and the environment default.

A keyless LlmAdapter that emits one reasoning block plus a shell tool call on the first request and a text answer once a tool result is present, so a CLI smoke can prove a real tool round trip without a provider key.
Three-line subprocess fixture that writes 'fixture failed' to stderr and exits 7, for the non-zero-exit smoke case.
Subprocess fixture that prints and then holds the event loop open with a 1 s interval, for the deadline-kill smoke case.

Snapshot-only Loader driver: boots the shipped headless profile over a test overlay, optionally awaits a required Loader entry's activation, runs one fixture turn, and streams every canonical session event as JSONL to stdout.

bootProductionProfile: loads a shipped profile's bundle layers, layers *.patch.yml test overlays above them, computes the runtime resolution, and boots through production boot() with a profileContext carrying the launcher's own profile facts.
Subprocess fixture that echoes argv, execArgv, cwd, DSH_HOME, DSH_AGENTS_HOME, an env marker and the consumed stdin as one JSON line, then writes 'fixture stderr' to stderr.

Spec for runLoaderSmoke: process isolation with closed stdin, captured stdout/stderr, removed temp cwd, a caller-provided cwd left in place, arbitrary bin argv plus prepare/inspect hooks, the non-zero-exit diagnostic, a declared expected exit code that a clean run still fails, and the deadline kill reporting captured output.
tsconfig extending tsconfig.base.json with references to cordis, agent, llm, session and http-proxy.
Per-section en/zh digests for the test-support group map.
Group map for packages/test-support listing the seven packages (session-snapshot, agent-loop-testkit, client-runtime, remote-mock, loader-smoke, llm-mock-server, llm-replay) and their one-line roles.
Chinese mirror of the test-support group map.
Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-remote-mock: @vitest/spy as the only runtime dependency so the mock also works in a browser page; peers on cordis and dsh-typert-protocol.
Per-section en/zh digests for the remote-mock README (13 sections).

English doc for the endpoint-named Remote mock: the native-mock proxy surface, the default-response table, stream driving (frames/openStream, push/end/fail, opened/drained), connecting a client via mock.rpc, and the observation API (calls/streams/requests/unmatched/assertNoUnmatched).
Chinese mirror of the remote-mock README; same five known limits, including that values pass by reference and are not validated.

Public barrel: RemoteMock/ok, the OpenStreams and RemoteTable types, the frames/openStream/streamHandle/streamMethod script helpers, MockClientStream, the log types, and the MockedRemote alias; explicitly browser-safe (no DOM, React or Node imports).

MockLogStore: a shared seq counter across calls and stream opens, call entries that go pending -> answered/failed with the value or the thrown error, stream entries with a pushed count and open/ended/failed/cancelled state, and requests() that lists the first positional arg in seq order excluding $-prefixed endpoints.

RemoteMock: an endpoint table of unary answers and stream scripts, a native-mock proxy, a Connection carrier face (rpc.call / rpc.open over { args } payloads), a live-stream control surface, a global seq log, and assertNoUnmatched() at teardown.
createRemoteProxy: a two-level Proxy that lazily caches namespace/method identities and returns undefined for `then` and symbol probes, so the mock stays inert under await and enumeration.

Scriptable stream machinery: streamHandle/streamMethod for faking a generated stream method, frames/openStream script builders, MockStream (one consumer, a push queue, end/fail/cancel settling, a drained() promise) and MockClientStream (the uplink half with lossless-JSON send checks).

Type-level spec that compiles a synthetic Remote namespace map with the TypeScript compiler API to prove MockedRemote keeps namespace/method names and signatures and that the runtime proxy adds no import of the protocol or the spy package.

Spec for the native namespace mocks: identity caching, inert thenable/symbol probes, FIFO consumption of queued one-shot answers across direct and carrier calls, positional-argument recording, the carrier keeping its AbortSignal out of the args, and a failed stream rejecting the reader.

Spec for the Connection carrier face: payload shapes (array vs single object), the uplink handed to the script and kept out of the logged args, uplink close on stream end and on an early consumer exit, malformed payload and unmatched-endpoint rejection with the miss logged, and abort semantics.

Spec for stream scripts and live control: frames() then end, openStream() plus filtered push/end/fail with delivery counts, a single-consumer rule, settling twice as a no-op, cancellation recorded as cancelled, the $events ready frame per generation, and opened() waiting for N opens.

Spec for unary answers: fixed values logged with a global seq, default replacement and an explicit undefined answer, positional handlers, raw vs handler answers, the pending/answered/failed log states, and requests() ordering.
Client tsconfig extending tsconfig.base.client.json with references to typert/protocol, cordis and client/connection.
tsdown config reusing the shared clientLibrary() helper.

Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-snapshot: depends on the ACP SDK, cordis-plugin-include, dsh-llm-replay, dsh-loader-smoke, dsh-session-format, js-yaml and vitest; peers on cordis, dsh-session and dsh-http-proxy.
Per-section en/zh digests for the session-snapshot README (11 sections).

English doc for the keyless snapshot tier: the scenario-table-plus-factory-call shape, the closed snapshot.yml manifest and canonical parent/child filenames, record/replay/refresh modes, the header-class pinning rule and its sidecars, platform/permission/composition variants, and the limit that session harvest requires raw JSONL mode.
Chinese mirror of the session-snapshot README; same manifest, pinning and mode rules.

runScenario: boots the real agent bin through the Loader, drives it over real ACP JSON-RPC stdio with a deterministic input script (prompt, promptAndCancel, promptExpectError, waitForTurnStart/End, waitForGoalPhase, waitForInboxMessage, waitForSubagentTurnEnd, waitForTitleAfterTurnEnd, waitForEventAfterTurnEnd, waitForFile), tees raw stdout, harvests the persisted session JSONL, and records the run's outcome.

redactSessionSnapshotIds: relationship-preserving identity redaction that maps volatile UUIDs, short job ids, approval/command/rpc/retry/run ids and generic id keys to typed {{kind:n}} tokens, keeps equality across parent and child logs, and is a fixed point.

Public barrel of the snapshot kit: identity redaction, the scenario harness, the ACP launcher, the normalizers (stdout/session-log/prompt/tool-schema scrubbing, cwd tokenizing, spill-path extraction), the manifest parser, the session-filename helpers, the suite factory's pinning helpers, and the workspace capture.

launchAcpTestAgent: source-or-built spawn resolution, workspace env, stdout tee, an ACP SDK client, update collection, fail-closed permission handling and shutdown, plus materializeProfilePatch which rebases authored relative module names and links profile packages into the temp cwd.

parseSnapshotManifest: a closed YAML manifest parser (profile, composition, recording, header class/pin, replay override, platform, permission, environment, workspace, input/attachments, session reference, sessionFormat coverage) that rejects unknown keys and every bad shape with a labelled message; writesCurrentSessionFixtures decides who may write current fixtures.

All the pure normalizers: cwd/session-id/UUID scrubbing with path-boundary matching, canonical vs native separator modes, job/goal/feedback/subagent clock zeroing, the {{system}}/{{tools}} prompt and schema tokenizers, the session-log/stdout comparators, and the projection that drops persistence envelopes.

Canonical Session filename grammar: sessionFixtureName/parseSessionFixtureName/sessionFixtureFiles/sessionFixtureNames, persistedSessionFilename/parsePersistedSessionFilename/latestPersistedSessionPaths, and the filename-vs-header generation assertions; every non-negative-safe-integer check throws.

The suite factory: one scenario per header class pins the tokenized request-header and system/message sequences with readable sidecars, replay/record/refresh modes (replay runs concurrently, record/refresh stay serial while writing), the shared-snapshot claim/uniqueness rules, the refresh stabilization pass, the fixture storage guard, and the orphan/pin meta-tests.
Workspace capture: a path-stable, host-separator-independent snapshot of text, binary (base64), symlink and empty-directory entries, with the .empty marker excluded from the expected tree.
Loader fixture that throws on any user-questions/request, so a scenario proves a delegated question never reaches the UI answerer.
Loader fixture that appends a working-directory/change event to '/tmp' on agent creation, giving a fixed POSIX directory context for synthetic compaction recordings.

Loader fixture layering dynamic-tool-updates with a systemPrompt section that gains guidance after the first read, asserting that the second request keeps the first request's history and carries exactly two system messages.

Loader fixture registering a tool after a read and removing it after use, asserting through llm/stream that projectToolUpdates defers the new declaration until its chronological activation and that addition-only routes remove unavailable declarations and their activations.

Scripted fake ACP agent bin: every behavior comes from a behaviour.json beside the fixture, it echoes env/workspace/permission facts into session/update text chunks, it can park a prompt until session/cancel, it persists scripted logs (with {{CWD}}/{{SID}} substitution) on cancel and on stdin EOF, and it can leave stray files or a deleted sessions root for the harvester to skip.
Loader fixture that adds a systemPrompt section after the first successful read, so the next step renders a changed system prompt (an in-history prompt update).
Loader fixture that selects the 'parent' agent preset on every root Session at creation, before the agent/created publication checks.
Loader fixture that switches every root session to read-only at creation, so a continuable background child provably inherits the parent's explicit override as a delegation-sourced event.

Snapshot-only SandboxProvider whose default launch reproduces an older-ABI partial Landlock (exit 125 plus an informational line), and whose env-flagged variant points at a missing runner under the workspace cwd to exercise runner-failure classification.
Loader fixture that changes the session file policy to read-only from outside the active tool call while a nested tool awaits cancellation.
Behaviour script for the record-mode child scenario: a respond prompt plus two scripted v3 session logs (a parent and a child sharing the same system message id and the same inherited user message).
Input script for the record child scenario: initialize, newSession, prompt.
Historical v0 child fixture: a parent-linked session header with a request/header carrying {{system}}/{{tools}} and the inherited user message.
Historical v3 child fixture: turn/step events, a system/message, a request/header and the inherited user message, with typed {{session:n}}/{{message:n}} tokens and {{cwd}}.
Historical v0 parent fixture of the record child scenario: a session header plus the initial request/header and the user message.
Current-generation parent fixture of the record child scenario: v3 header, turn/step events, a system/message, a request/header and the user message.
Two-line closed manifest (version 1, profile acp) for the record child scenario.
Expected stdout of the record child scenario: the initialize result, the session/new result with {{sessionId}}, one agent_message_chunk and the end_turn response.
Child tool-schema sidecar: one initial schema (t1) and no changes.
Behaviour script for the record pin scenario: one scripted v3 session log with a system message and an initial request/header carrying tool t1.
Input script for the record pin scenario: initialize, newSession, prompt.
Historical v0 fixture of the record pin scenario, a session header plus one request/header.
Historical v0 parent fixture of the record pin scenario with a real (untokenized) cwd.
Current-generation parent fixture of the record pin scenario with typed tokens and {{cwd}}.
Two-line closed manifest (version 1, profile acp) for the record pin scenario.
Expected stdout of the record pin scenario: four NDJSON frames (initialize result, session/new, one chunk, end_turn).
Readable system-prompt sidecar holding the literal text 'SYS PROMPT'.
Tool-schema sidecar for the record pin scenario: one initial schema (t1) and no changes.
Empty behaviour object for the skip scenario (no prompt, no logs).
Input script for the skip scenario: initialize only.
Override sidecar with a single hang entry, forcing the replayed model call to stall until cancelled.
One-line header-only session fixture for the skip scenario.
Two-line closed manifest (version 1, profile acp) for the skip scenario.
Expected stdout of the skip scenario: only the initialize result frame.

Loader fixture that holds child execution until the parent's turn has closed, then updates the subagent Loader entry's config to maxActiveSubagents 1 so the capacity probe is recorded deterministically.

Loader fixture that remaps an authored placeholder child id to the live child, fences the unknown-child persistence stat behind both accepted follow-ups, forces a fixed durability-checkpoint failure on the child's final continuation turn, and can fail a published child's follow-up and disposal independently.

Loader fixture registering a SubagentProvider that returns four fixed product-failure diagnostics (with and without partial output) and then a fifth start whose result succeeds while its disposal throws, proving the parent sees the answer and the cleanup failure separately.

Loader fixture that holds the child until the parent's spawn turn ends and then parks the parent until the child's settlement notice has been inserted, so replay scheduling cannot fold settlement into the parent's first turn.
Loader fixture that awaits ctx.subagents.waitForChildren after any subagent tool call, holding the tool response until activation settlement has queued its notice.

Loader fixture registering a subagent_structured tool with a fixed output schema, which sends a correction to the child through subagents.sendMessage before the child submits its structured answer and then awaits the activation result.
Behaviour script for the authored-error scenario: a prompt that errors, plus a scripted v3 log whose turn/end carries the error reason.
Input script for the authored-error scenario: initialize, newSession, promptExpectError.
Override sidecar with a zero-chunk throw entry carrying message 'model exploded' and code PROVIDER.
Historical v0 authored-error fixture: a session header plus a bare turn/end with an error string.
Historical v2 authored-error fixture: a session header, a turn/start and a turn/end carrying the structured error reason.
Two-line closed manifest (version 1, profile acp) for the authored-error scenario.
Expected stdout of the authored-error scenario: initialize, session/new, one chunk, then a JSON-RPC error frame with message 'model exploded'.
Behaviour script for the blocked-log scenario: an erroring prompt plus a scripted v3 log containing a hook/result with decision 'block' and a duration.
Input script for the blocked-log scenario: initialize, newSession, promptExpectError.
Historical v0 blocked-log fixture: a session header plus a hook/result with decision block.
Historical v2 blocked-log fixture: a session header plus a full hook/result record (turn, point, handlerId, decision, durationMs).
Two-line closed manifest (version 1, profile acp) for the blocked-log scenario.
Expected stdout of the blocked-log scenario: four frames ending in a JSON-RPC error frame, identical in shape to the authored-error golden.
Empty behaviour object for the no-model scenario.
Input script for the no-model scenario: initialize only.
One-line header-only session fixture for the no-model scenario.
Two-line closed manifest (version 1, profile acp) for the no-model scenario.
